excerpt: Blunt force trauma can be severe with no symptoms at first. The warning signs after a crash, and why delayed treatment hurts both health and a claim.

faqs.question: What is blunt force trauma?
faqs.answer: An injury caused by a sudden impact or collision with an object rather than by something penetrating the body. They can be serious even when the skin is not broken, because the damage is often internal.

faqs.question: Why is blunt force trauma so dangerous?
faqs.answer: Because initially there may be no symptoms at all. These injuries are tricky and can escalate quickly to become life-threatening without immediate medical attention, which is why they can be missed at the scene.

faqs.question: Can blunt force trauma injuries be fatal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Internal bleeding, organ damage and traumatic brain injury from a blunt impact can be fatal, particularly when the injury goes unrecognized because the person seemed uninjured and was not examined after the crash.

faqs.question: What symptoms should I watch for after a crash?
faqs.answer: Any developing pain, swelling, dizziness, confusion, worsening headache, repeated vomiting, abdominal tenderness or shortness of breath in the hours and days afterward. Symptoms that appear late are exactly the pattern that makes these injuries dangerous. Call 911 or go to an emergency department if symptoms are severe or getting worse.

faqs.question: When should I seek medical attention after a Savannah crash?
faqs.answer: Immediately, and regardless of how you feel at the scene. Immediate medical attention could be life-saving, and your medical records also help document the link between the collision and the injuries that follow.

metaDescription: Blunt force trauma from a Savannah crash can cause internal injuries before symptoms appear. Learn the warning signs and why to see a doctor right away.
